items.p: A local Customer Success Manager desk. One operator, many customer books. Tickets, mail, Slack, Teams, Salesforce, and calendar sit on one account so you do not reply to the wrong company.
Every book has a color chip and a 2–6 character abbreviation. They follow every row, tile, and chat so ACME and NORTHWIND never mix.

Home opens on Agenda. Left: meetings for the selected day (arrows change the day). Right: new email, Slack, Teams, and tasks, newest first. The + in that pane creates a task — a mail to yourself. Subject is Tasks: Company : name {type}. CC uses people from the selected company. AI Assist drafts the name, due date, CC, and body from that book and the type you picked. The body holds the note and When Due By.

Companies shows one tile per book: health, next meeting, and counts for new tickets, email, Slack/Teams, and calendar invites. Click a tile to open that book in the left pane. Chat stays on the right and is scoped to that book.
The right pane is always chat. On Home it covers the whole desk. With a book open it is only about that account. Ask things like “Is there any issue with #{ACME}?” or “Did @bob from #{ACME} reply?”
The three icons at the top of chat are History (earlier threads), Bookmark (pin this one), and New chat (clean thread). Hover an icon for its name.
Type in the account search to filter the current tab. Start with / to jump types: /note, /project, /people, /email, /ticket, /slack, /teams, /calendar, /sf.

Compose drafts from tickets, recent mail, Slack, Teams, and calendar. Grok writes when a key is present; otherwise a template is saved. Open a thread and click Suggest reply for a draft on that conversation. Send is off in this version.
Open a timeline card and assign a project. That is how mail, tickets, Slack, Teams, and Salesforce land on the right book of work.
A person can belong to one or more projects. Add or edit them on People, the org chart, or Account team. Directors can own every project — check All projects, or type /project all.

On Projects, search or filter by type and status — a book can have hundreds. Add project opens a form: type, status, an owner from the people list, an optional group email, and tags (type and press Enter). Click a row to edit or remove it.
Besides projects, tag a person Ops, Accounting, or DBA — or leave them untagged. Search finds those labels.

Click the digital clock above Desk chat to open the converter. Search a city (Los Angeles, even “las angoles”), add or remove rows, and drag the handle to reorder. Hover a column to compare; click two hours to mark a meeting window. Your timezone is the You row. Picks are saved in the local database and survive refresh and restart.
Name, phone, email, and timezone live under You. Mail from your domain is treated as internal. The timezone pins the You row on the world clock and drives Agenda’s idea of today.

Add a customer book. Quiet hides it from Home. Remove archives it. Edit to set color, crop a logo, and map domains plus Slack, Teams, Salesforce, and Jira tags so inbound mail lands on the right book.
Keys stay in data/secrets.json (mode 0600). Compose uses Grok when that key is present. Connector mode lives in config.json; Test checks health and auth.
Load seed data writes three books: ACME (navy), NWIN (forest), GLX (burgundy). Seed is idempotent. Reset wipes books and keeps your settings, including the world clock.
